verdict.rationale: Cursor documents a first-party Privacy Mode under which code is never used for training by Cursor or other AI model providers, and it is on by default for Enterprise teams. That covers the core of the opt-out. The docs only explicitly mention code, not prompts, and do not describe how a lead turns the setting on for non-Enterprise plans. They also note that Zero Data Retention does not apply when you use your own API keys. Missing for 10: explicit coverage of prompts, documented opt-out/enforcement steps for non-Enterprise teams, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can opt out of having my code and prompts used for AI model training

citations.quote: With Privacy Mode enabled your code is never used for training by Cursor or other AI model providers.
Privacy Mode is on by default for Enterprise teams.
Zero Data Retention "does not apply when you use your own API keys."
